clue.text: Without love, beast has to hurt, so droop faced?

definitions.note: read as 'with a droop on the face', describing the long drooping style of facial hair

parts.note: the walrus is a large tusked sea beast

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the phrase for 'has to hurt' wraps around the letter for love

parts.note: has to = must, hurt = ache, giving the phrase must ache
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sad creature, hurting so much that its face sags in misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside: MUST ACHE goes around O to give MOUSTACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: This bushy facial-hair style hangs down over the mouth like a sea mammal's whiskers, so a face wearing one droops.

clue.text: No one remaining hairy in sports? Be careful what you say!

indicators.note: the shaving phrase is placed inside the word for sports

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them, so sports means wears
if nobody stays hairy then all shave

explanation.surface: Everyone in a sports team has gone clean-shaven, and someone warns against gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' looks like games but is the verb meaning wears; W...EARS wraps ALL SHAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that someone may be eavesdropping, an idiomatic caution to guard your words.

clue.text: Foot part raised, carried in fat gymnast's stretcher

indicators.note: the reversed foot part is held inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns its letters upwards so it reads backwards

parts.note: a toe is part of the foot

explanation.surface: A gymnast lifts a foot and is carried off on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' is not the medical one but a stretchy garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast's close-fitting stretchy one-piece garment, wittily called a stretcher because it stretches.

clue.text: Without knowing, white unicorn's heading up to god

indicators.note: the heading of the unicorn is its first letter
in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: wan means pale or white-faced
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A white unicorn's horn points up towards a god, unbeknown to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ares is the Greek god of war; 'up' applies to the word for white only.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught off guard is to be taken unprepared, without being aware; an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Tongue a degree pronounced, cut

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: pronounced means said

explanation.surface: A language with a degree of pronunciation that has been clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and this is the language of an East African pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: A round end is round, plain and simple

indicators.note: round as in going round, turning about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some circular thing whose end is also circular, described as plain and simple.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'round' signals the anagram of A ROUND END.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without decoration or ornament is plain and simple, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tone with which doctor plugs drain

indicators.note: the doctor fills a gap in the word for drain, like a plug in a hole

parts.note: to drain someone is to tire them out
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A tone of voice, and a doctor stopping up a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' looks like a sink outlet but is the verb meaning tire.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive quality of a sound or voice is its tone; a music term for tone colour.

clue.text: Party with two runners?

parts.note: a car is a runner (a used-car dealer's 'good runner') and the Ouse, an English river, runs; together they make a word meaning to party

explanation.surface: A party with two people running, perhaps a relay team.
explanation.walkthrough: The two runners are a motor car and the Ouse, a river in England; side by side they spell a verb meaning to party.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink and make merry noisily is to party, and the word splits into a vehicle and a river.

clue.text: Our home is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that where we live is a dump.
explanation.walkthrough: A fox lives in an earth, its burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet, and also the burrow where a fox lives, two separate senses of the same word.

clue.text: Dessert knocked over, drunk has dried fruit

indicators.note: knocked over means the word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a creamy fruit dessert

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of has stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A pudding gets upset and a tipsy diner has some dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dried fruit' suggests raisins, but a loofah is the dried fibrous fruit of a gourd. FOOL backwards gives LOOF; HAS jumbled gives AHS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath sponge is the dried fibrous interior of a gourd's fruit, so dried fruit is literally true.

clue.text: Male ensnared by a more dreadful lover

indicators.note: the male letter is trapped inside the phrase

parts.note: a + direr, direr meaning more dreadful

explanation.surface: A man caught by an even worse lover, a sorry romantic tale.
explanation.definitionFit: One who loves or adores someone, a synonym for a fan or suitor.

clue.text: Springboks not quite heard?

parts.note: split the first word as Spring + boks: spring is the definition, and boks heard is box

explanation.surface: South Africa's rugby team almost going unheard.
explanation.walkthrough: Springboks are South Africa's rugby team. Split the word: 'Spring' defines; 'boks' heard is 'box', i.e. SPAR, and 'not quite' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral spring, or a resort built around one, so the word means a spring.

clue.text: Suggestion of a fit body, not half! Lady Chatterley's Lover, possibly?

indicators.note: made of, so the letters that follow are reworked into a new form
not half means half of the word body is lost, leaving its front

parts.note: a rough is a preliminary sketch, a mere suggestion of the finished work

explanation.surface: A hint of a toned physique, and how! Perhaps the famous lover from Lawrence's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' sounds like the British exclamation of hearty agreement but halves BODY to BO; A FIT BO rearranged gives A BIT OF. The signals are loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellors, the gamekeeper in Lawrence's novel, is the classic lower-class lover of a lady: British slang for such a man.

clue.text: Dealing with commercial arrangement

parts.note: a TV commercial is an ad
dressing is arrangement, as in window dressing

explanation.surface: Handling a business arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with a problem is to tackle or attend to it, a synonymous verb phrase.

clue.text: Sucker has wee in lift during comedy routine

indicators.note: the lifted word comes during, inside, the comedy routine

parts.note: shtick is a comedian's routine or gimmick

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: wee and pee both mean urine

explanation.surface: A gross comedy routine where someone wets themselves in a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe but is a bloodsucking parasite of flocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite that sucks blood from flocks of sheep, so it is literally a sucker.

clue.text: Combination locks, late '70s style?

definitions.meaning: a permutation, as in a football pools entry choosing combinations
curled hair from a chemical treatment, fashionable in the late 1970s

explanation.surface: A combination lock, or a hairstyle from the end of the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks are hair, not padlocks. A perm on the football pools (a British betting game) is a set of combinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for permutation, a combination; and short for permanent wave, a curly hairdo.

clue.text: One in twelve boxes unsatisfactory, one tiny part

indicators.note: the month encloses the other letters as if in a box

parts.note: a month is one of the twelve in a year
ill means bad or unsatisfactory, as in ill-advised
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One box in twelve is faulty, a tiny fraction of the batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in twelve' looks like a fraction but is MONTH, which boxes ILL and I.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in a very large number, so a minute fraction of a whole.

clue.text: Minister and earls surprisingly backing movement

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a minister

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of earls fall into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A clergyman and some aristocrats unexpectedly support a political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing movement' reads as supporting a campaign, but means a backward move.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn in the opposite direction, a going back, so a backwards motion.

clue.text: See 1 down
Queen binds princess up, then knight captured again

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the letters bottom to top, backwards
the queen's letters wrap around the princess's name

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina
Kate, the Princess of Wales
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: The Queen ties up a princess and then a knight takes a piece again, chess-like.
explanation.walkthrough: EKATER read upwards gives RETAKE, then N.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture something is to take it back once more, a synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Comic called in about exercise for writer

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the exercise
comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: A comedian is summoned about some exercise for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author but is the implement; 'Comic' shuffles CALLED IN to LEADNCIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphite writing implement, so a tool that writes, old-fashioned name for an ordinary pencil.

clue.text: Similar drinks brought together with classy French wine

parts.note: cha and tea are two words for the same drink
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Similar drinks are combined with a smart French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a British label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for a château-bottled wine from a Bordeaux estate, a wine named after its estate house.

clue.text: Musical creation of Sullivan, The Mikado

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A work by Sullivan, who wrote The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: Sullivan composed The Mikado with Gilbert, so the surface reads naturally. Look inside sulliVAN THE Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of praise or a national song, a piece of music created for singing.

clue.text: Dante acts up, spoiling writer's moving technique

indicators.note: spoiling the order of these letters breaks them up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The poet Dante misbehaves, ruining an author's emotional technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acts up' is part of the fodder, not a reversal signal. 'moving' means relocating text, not touching.
explanation.definitionFit: A word-processing method of relocating text, so an author's way of shifting passages.

clue.text: By which one might recognise a prize archer?

parts.note: a cup is a sporting prize
ID, identification, is how one is recognised

explanation.surface: How one might spot a champion bowman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the ID of a prize: CUP then ID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is shown as a winged boy firing love's arrows.

clue.text: Power company after ultimate in riches

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of riches

parts.note: a team is a company of people working together

explanation.surface: A powerful firm that follows the very top in wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Water vapour drove engines in the industrial age, so it is a source of power.

clue.text: He fought a wild animal — that's not on

indicators.note: the word on is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: a + lion, a wild big cat

explanation.surface: A man battled a wild beast, which was unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not on' looks like a British phrase for unfair, but removes ON from A LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad, the famous heavyweight boxing champion, was a fighter by trade.

clue.text: Asian leaves house in mid-Sicily after Corleone initially quits mob

indicators.note: after places the mob piece first, with the Sicilian part following it
the initial letter leaves the word for mob

parts.note: a pack is a mob or gang

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the name Corleone
the house letters sit inside the central part of Sicily
mid takes the central letters of Sicily

explanation.surface: An Asian man leaves his house in central Sicily after the Godfather's family quits the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun, foliage. Corleone is the Godfather's family.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese leafy vegetable, so Asian leaves in the salad or stir-fry sense.

clue.text: One Direction's festival season's ending

definitions.note: read as 'belonging to one compass direction', an adjective

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the ending of season is its last letter

explanation.surface: The boy band One Direction's festive season comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction was a British boy band; here it is one compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the point where the sun rises, one of the four compass directions.

clue.text: I must remain serious, you're joking!

definitions.meaning: a plea not to be set off giggling

explanation.surface: Someone trying to keep a straight face while scoffing at an absurd claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a request not to be amused; idiomatically a sarcastic retort meaning that's ridiculous.
